static_traits.name: Li Ming
static_traits.social_status: Has friends and family to discuss daily matters with, but hesitates to express insecurity and failure
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness, no similar psychological problems or treatment history in the past
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, able to describe automatic thoughts and emotions, highly cooperative, positive attitude; but often uses absolutist and catastrophizing expressions (e.g. 'I am a failure', 'without a luxury car one is not successful')

basic_info.main_problem: I persistently feel insecure and like a failure because I believe owning material possessions like an expensive Corvette counts as success. Comparison raises the pressure; I work overtime trying to afford the car, affecting relationships with family and mental health. Almost daily, when seeing others own luxury goods, these feelings of failure and insecurity get activated.
basic_info.core_demands: I decided to seek counseling because these feelings of inadequacy and failure are affecting my relationships with family and causing significant stress.

core_beliefs: My worth depends on whether I own expensive material things and external achievements

special_situations.event: Seeing peers or others own expensive cars (such as a Corvette) and other luxuries
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I have no luxury car or other symbols of success, I do not count as successful, which equals failure
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Works overtime and researches car loans, trying to prove his own worth by buying a luxury car
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Without a luxury car I am just a failure / I will never succeed

special_situations.event: At work, repeatedly calculates how much more money is needed to afford a luxury car
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot earn enough money to buy the luxury car, I will let my family down and accomplish nothing
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Extends working hours, focusing energy on making money and loan plans
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: If I cannot earn money to buy the car, I will disappoint my family, and things will get worse and worse

special_situations.event: Noticing that relationships with one's wife and children have become strained due to long-term overtime work and stress
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If family relationships worsen, it is because I do not meet the 'successful provider' standard
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Invests further in work, trying to compensate for relationship problems with material things; reduces quality time with family
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I failed as a provider; the worsened relationship is all my fault

special_situations.event: Feeling embarrassed when thinking of discussing insecurity and failure with friends or family
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I expose vulnerability and anxiety, others will look down on me and deem me unworthy
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoids expressing vulnerability and seeking support from people around her, keeping silent
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They will think I am useless, very shameful

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be recognized by family and others, to be seen as successful and loved as a provider
core_conflict.fear: Fearing being seen as a failure, being humiliated or looked down upon, thus losing worth and relationships
defense_goal: Through overtime work and pursuing material achievements, relieving shame and insecurity
Avoiding expressing vulnerability, maintaining surface control to protect self-esteem
Measures the self by external standards to gain a sense of certainty

object_relations.self_representation: An incompetent provider falling short of standards
object_relations.object_representation: Family members who would be disappointed and might judge me

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When encouraged to express insecurity and vulnerability to family or friends, or when counseling focuses on shame and failure
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Believing exposing vulnerability equals losing face and being looked down upon or rejected
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Responds in objective, factual language, avoids first-person emotion words, restrained in tone, reduces emotional details.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor challenges rigid standards such as 'success = owning a luxury car' or explores the source of their values
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Experiencing one's efforts and identity as negated, needing to prove oneself right with rationality
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Turns to discussing details such as data, loan interest rates, income, and budgets, replacing emotional expression with logical deduction, tone calm.

manifestations: Simplifies 'success' into material possession (such as luxury cars), measuring self-worth by external standards
In comparison, gradually overlooks relationship quality with the wife and children and one's own well-being
outcomes: Increased work pressure and fatigue, decreased life satisfaction

manifestations: Feeling embarrassed and hesitant about expressing insecurity and failure to friends and family
Chooses to work overtime alone under pressure rather than seek support
outcomes: Emotional isolation and underutilized support systems

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Treating 'owning a luxury car counts as success' as an unquestionable standard
Uses the luxury goods others own as the core basis for self-evaluation

contact_model.definition: The individual restrains the impulse to act on others, and instead does it to herself, consuming energy inwardly, corresponding to 'impulse'.
manifestations: Not seeking help from family and friends or expressing vulnerability, instead continuing overtime and self-depletion
Replacing direct communication and negotiation with others with self-harshness

positive_force: Family love and support (wife and children love him)
Works hard, has a sense of responsibility
Clear motivation to seek help, positive attitude, willing to try cognitive restructuring
Able to identify negative automatic thoughts and try more balanced views
negative_force: Overly relies on external validation and social comparison to assess self-worth
Cognitive distortions such as catastrophizing and black-and-white thinking are salient
Shame and avoidance of vulnerability reduce the support obtained from relationships
Long-term overtime causing fatigue and relationship estrangement, further reinforcing the negative cycle

target_behavior.behavior: Overworks (long-term overtime) in pursuit of buying a luxury car
antecedent: Seeing others own luxury cars and other luxuries
At work, repeatedly calculates the money needed and worries about affordability
target_behavior.core_reason: Binding self-worth to material success in an introjected way, producing catastrophizing and external-validation needs out of fear of being seen as a failure
target_behavior.function: Escaping shame and insecurity, temporarily gaining a sense of control and expecting external recognition
target_behavior.consequence: Increased stress and fatigue, decline in work performance, tense family relationships, lower quality of life

target_behavior.behavior: Avoiding expressing insecurity to family or friends (emotional avoidance)
antecedent: Thinking of discussing one's sense of failure and anxiety
When asked about his recent situation or when focusing on emotions in counseling
target_behavior.core_reason: Worries about being judged and shame; believes exposing vulnerability equals losing face
target_behavior.function: Escaping feelings of being negated and humiliated, protecting fragile self-esteem
target_behavior.consequence: Emotional isolation, underutilized support systems, insecurity and a persistent sense of failure possibly worsening

target_behavior.behavior: Repeated social comparison and self-deprecation by material standards
antecedent: Sees peers' or others' luxury goods in real-life/social settings
Contact with topics and media content about 'standards of success'
target_behavior.core_reason: Introjecting the rigid rule of 'success = material', externalized dependence in self-worth evaluation
target_behavior.function: (Attempts) to locate the self through comparison and seek external confirmation
target_behavior.consequence: Worsened anxiety and inferiority, more negative automatic thoughts, further triggering overtime and relationship avoidance
